newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Goldman Sachs buys 9.1 pct of Hung Hing.
newsitem.headline: Goldman Sachs buys 9.1 pct of Hung Hing.

text.p: Goldman Sachs & Co said on Wednesday it had acquired 47.6 million new shares in Hung Hing Printing Group at HK$3.60 each, giving it a 9.1 percent stake in the Hong Kong printing packaging company.

"We are interested in Hung Hing because the company has exciting growth prospects, solid management and domestic business in China," Henry Cornell, managing director of the privately-held investment bank, said of the HK$171.5 million investment.
The Yam family will remain the largest shareholder of the company with a 30 percent stake after the new share issue.
Hung Hing said the proceeds of the issue would be used to invest in a plant in Zhongshan in China's southern Guangdong province and another plant in Fuyong in Shenzhen.
Trading in Hung Hing shares was suspended on Wednesday. The stock closed at HK$4.375 on Tuesday.
Hung Hing had a net profit of HK$107.06 million in the year ended March 31, 1996, up from HK$73.27 million the year before.
